title: A textbook says very young infants already react to how objects behave
summary: OpenStax Psychology says researchers found that very young infants understand how objects behave sooner than Piaget's timetable allowed.
body: OpenStax Psychology says Piaget thought understanding objects, such as a rattle making noise when shaken, developed slowly as a child matured and met the world. The chapter says developmental psychologists now think that timetable was too slow. It points to work in which children as young as 3 months showed knowledge of object properties they had only viewed, not handled for a long time. The page is one textbook's reading of that research, published 8 December 2014. It is not a checklist for a particular child, and the truck procedure itself is a separate card.
